resources.string: C-cell icons moved toward a vessel
Icons still inside the C-cell sketch: %1$s
Icons moved = rows × icons moved per row. Icons still inside = rows × (5 − icons moved per row). The chart rounds the controls to whole numbers.

Thyroid parafollicular cells (C cells) lie in the outer part of the follicular wall or between follicles. They release calcitonin into the blood, not into the colloid-filled follicle. In this sketch, five icons start in each row inside the C cell. The same number moves from each row toward a nearby vessel on the tissue side. The grid and counts are invented and do not represent real granule counts, secretion rates, or blood levels.
